text: {"lessons":["Selling Stock B, E and D mainly because they were above my cost—and later selling A and C at steep losses—shows I need consistent, forward-looking reasons to trade, not the emotional comfort of locking in gains or avoiding a realized loss.","I sold A and C and then bought them back, sometimes adding more later. Before any trade, I should check whether new information or a sound valuation justifies it, rather than reacting to price moves or trying to undo an earlier decision.","Repeatedly buying all five stocks without a clear portfolio plan can use cash inefficiently and ignore changing risk. I should set allocation and review rules, then trade only when a position or the overall portfolio warrants it."]}
